answer: A strong defence is a staking-plus-attestation system: each agent must lock a bond and publish a signed cipher commitment tied to a verified identity record. A shared prism of reputation data lets peers score behaviour across many interactions instead of trusting a single claim, so fake accounts cannot copy a good history cheaply. A beacon service then issues fresh random challenges that agents must answer with their bonded key; cheap clones fail the challenge or lose their stake, making large-scale Sybil creation economically unprofitable.
